summary: Island Lake Airport serves the remote Island Lake community in northern Manitoba, providing a critical air link for several surrounding First Nations communities including Garden Hill and Wasagamack. As a medium-sized airport with no permanent all-weather road connecting it to the rest of the province, it is a lifeline for passengers, mail, and medical evacuations. The airport handles scheduled regional flights and is especially busy during seasonal transitions when winter and ice roads are not operational.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly to Island Lake Airport?
A: Calm Air and Perimeter Aviation provide scheduled passenger service, primarily connecting Island Lake to Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport.

Q: Are there road connections to Island Lake?
A: No permanent all-weather road exists; the community is accessible mainly by air year-round and by winter or ice roads during the colder months.

Q: Does the airport have customs or immigration facilities?
A: No, Island Lake Airport is a domestic airport serving only flights within Canada and does not have customs or immigration services.

Q: What is the airport used for besides passenger travel?
A: The airport supports medical evacuations, cargo deliveries, mail service, and government operations for the surrounding remote communities.
transport_tips: The airport is a short drive from the Island Lake community centre, and local taxi services or pre-arranged rides are the most common way to reach it. Passengers should confirm flight times in advance, as weather-related delays are common in northern Manitoba. There is no public transit serving the airport, so arranging ground transport ahead of time is recommended.
